run.question:
Customers reported slow checkout for the last hour. Check our Datadog APM
traces for the checkout-service and find which downstream call is slow.

report.summary: The question asks which downstream call of checkout is slow, but no trace or latency metric could be read in this Run: the Datadog APM source named in the request is not one of the available integrations (the available trace backend is Jaeger under target m0-otel-20260909), and every Jaeger and Prometheus query attempted returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, while Elasticsearch returned no indices. So no checkout span, operation duration or rpc client latency series was obtained, and no downstream call can be named as slow. What could be observed from the cluster and pod logs does not single out a dependency: all 21 Deployments in namespace otel-demo (including checkout, payment, shipping, cart, currency, quote, product-catalog, email) reported 1 ready / 1 available / 1 updated replica, all 22 pods in the namespace were Running, the only event whose timestamp fell inside the authorized window concerned Endpoints "loki" in namespace app-282 (FailedToCreateEndpoint, 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z), and the flagd fault-injection ConfigMap read at 06:26:37Z had every fault flag at defaultVariant "off". In the sampled checkout stdout log (newest 100 of 288 lines, 06:01:40-06:24:36) the order sequences show payment and confirmation email completing within roughly 10-30 ms of the [PlaceOrder] line, which is counter-evidence that those two downstream steps were slow in the sampled orders, but the cart, product-catalog, currency, quote/shipping and ship-order calls are not timed in the logs. Root cause is therefore left null; the specific slow downstream call remains unknown.

claims.text: All 21 Deployments in namespace otel-demo reported readyReplicas=1, availableReplicas=1 and updatedReplicas=1, including checkout, payment, shipping, cart, currency, quote, product-catalog, email and frontend.

All 22 pods in namespace otel-demo were in phase Running, including checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n, payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d, shipping-6fc5f694db-9sq2c, cart-549b8757d-zjgcd, currency-6db8974b78-8g7s7, quote-75774ddb4c-kpbqh and product-catalog-777f5468d4-hc8rj.

Pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n (owner ReplicaSet checkout-6578865d87) had restartCount 1 with lastState.terminated exitCode 255, reason "Unknown", startedAt 2026-11-20T16:32:37Z and finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z, i.e. before the authorized incident window began at 05:26:18Z; the pod was Ready and Running when read.

checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n stdout shows repeated successful order sequences; for example [PlaceOrder] at 2026-11-21T06:03:35.133654147Z, "payment went through" at 06:03:35.152842555Z and "order confirmation email sent" at 06:03:35.164181720Z, with similar sub-30 ms spacing at 06:08:30.425/06:08:30.444/06:08:30.454 and 06:24:33.677/06:24:33.690/06:24:33.698.

ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo (key demo.flagd.json, read at 2026-11-21T06:26:37Z) declares flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, each with state ENABLED and defaultVariant "off" (kafkaQueueProblems and loadGeneratorFloodHomepage default variant value 0).

The only event whose own timestamp lay inside the authorized window was an Endpoints event for name "loki" in namespace app-282, reason FailedToCreateEndpoint, message "Failed to create endpoint for service app-282/loki: endpoints \"loki\" already exists", lastTimestamp 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z; 19 further events had timestamps outside the window and were dropped.

The sampled checkout log does not show the payment charge or the confirmation email as slow downstream steps: in each sampled order the gap from the [PlaceOrder] line to "payment went through" is about 10-20 ms and to "order confirmation email sent" about another 10 ms; the cart, product-catalog, currency, quote and ship-order calls are not timed in these lines, so this counter-evidence covers only the two downstream steps that are logged with timestamps.

No flagd fault flag was enabled in flagd-config as read at 06:26:37Z (all defaultVariant values "off"), so that read gives no support for a flagd-injected cart, payment, product-catalog or recommendation fault; because the ConfigMap was read after the window and flagd can be overridden at runtime, the in-window flag state is not established by it.

Because no checkout span or rpc latency series could be read, the slow downstream call is still unidentified; the unmeasured segments of checkout's PlaceOrder path (cart read from cart/valkey-cart, product-catalog lookups, currency conversion, quote/shipping quote and ShipOrder) remain equally unsupported candidates. A Jaeger trace of a checkout PlaceOrder span, or rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_bucket broken down by rpc_service and rpc_method for service_name="checkout", would discriminate between them.

gaps: Datadog APM is not an available data source in this Run; the only trace backend exposed is Jaeger (target m0-otel-20260909), and every Jaeger call attempted (traces_list_services, traces_list_operations, traces_search on service "checkout" for 05:26:18-06:26:18 and for 06:21:18-06:26:18, traces_search_by_tags) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no checkout trace, span or operation duration was obtained.

Every Prometheus call attempted against target m0-otel-20260909 returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (get_metric_names, get_all_labels, get_series for traces_span_metrics_calls_total, execute_prometheus_instant_query twice, metrics_range_query for traces_span_metrics_calls_total and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_bucket), so no checkout call rate and no rpc client duration histogram/quantile for checkout or any dependency is known.
Elasticsearch index listing with pattern "*" returned no indices (no_data), so there is no searchable log index for this window; all log evidence here came from pod stdout via the Kubernetes API.

Whether a service literally named "checkout-service" exists in the trace backend was not verifiable, because the Jaeger service list could not be read; the cluster objects are named "checkout" (Deployment, ReplicaSet checkout-6578865d87, pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n).

The checkout log read was capped at the newest 100 of 288 matching lines covering 06:01:40-06:24:36; the portion of the window 05:26:18-06:01:40 was not read, so earlier orders (including any slow ones) are unknown.

Per-call durations for checkout's cart, product-catalog, currency, quote/shipping and ShipOrder dependencies are not present in the checkout stdout lines, and the filtered error/timeout searches on shipping, payment, quote, cart and currency pod logs returned no matching lines from views with status no_data, which proves neither health nor absence of errors for those pods.

Whether the reported customer-facing slowness is visible in the application at all was not established: no frontend request-latency or error signal could be read (frontend pod log filter 'checkout|error|slow|timeout' returned nothing in a no_data view, and frontend HTTP metrics were unavailable on the Prometheus source).
flagd flag overrides during the window are unknown; only the static flagd-config ConfigMap content read at 06:26:37Z was seen, and flagd may apply runtime overrides.

Most otel-demo pods showed restartCount 1 in the pod table; only checkout's previous termination was inspected (exitCode 255, reason "Unknown", 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z, before the window). Other pods' restart timings and reasons were not inspected.
next_steps: Restore or verify connectivity to the Jaeger and Prometheus backends for target m0-otel-20260909, then pull checkout PlaceOrder traces and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_bucket split by rpc_service/rpc_method for service_name="checkout" over 05:26-06:26 to identify the slow downstream call.
If Datadog APM is the intended source of truth, confirm whether an APM integration can be added to this Run's data sources; its absence is not evidence about service health.

Compare checkout client-span durations against the corresponding server spans in cart, product-catalog, currency, quote/shipping and payment to separate network/client-side delay from dependency-side processing.
Re-read flagd's runtime flag state (not only the static ConfigMap) for the incident window before drawing any conclusion about fault injection.
